text.text: The school office in one place: class sections and rooms, school events, teacher absences that need cover, and the requests staff send to the front office. Start each morning with the Dashboard and the Needs cover view. Keep student names out of this workspace; it is for staff and logistics only.
Every class section with its teacher, room and size, so the front office always knows where everyone is.
Assemblies, field trips, conferences and fairs, with who leads each and what it needs.
Teacher absences and who is covering each one.
Repairs, supplies, room set-ups and questions staff send to the office.
The school at a glance. Charts read the live tables.

cells.text: Class size limit minus students enrolled, never below zero
Use it when a new family enrolls; do not exceed the limit without the principal
Absences for the section marked Needs cover or Covered
A section with many absences may need a longer-term plan
No event is Confirmed until the notice has gone home

text.text: The first hour sets the day. Doing the same things in the same order means nothing is missed.
Open Absences and cover and book substitutes for every row marked Needs cover
Check Office requests for anything Urgent
Read the day's events and confirm rooms and staff
Put the day's changes on the staff board
Reconcile attendance with the student information system.
Call families of students absent without notice, following school policy.
Log any new requests that arrive at the desk.
Events go well when families hear early and staff know their role. Start six weeks ahead for anything with buses or food.

cells.text: Add the event, pick a lead and book the space or bus
Confirm staff cover and permission slips
Send the family notice and tick the box on the event
Check supplies, walk the route and brief staff
Mark done and note what to change next time

text.text: Accessibility for every family and student.
Allergies and dietary needs for any food.
A rain plan for outdoor events.
A substitute walking into a prepared room has a good day. One walking into a surprise does not.
A seating chart and bell schedule.
Lesson plans for each period and where materials are.
Names of two nearby teachers who can help.
Notes on students who need support, kept private and brief.
Book the substitute and press Mark covered.
Tell the front desk who is in which room.
Collect feedback from the substitute at the end of the day.
